plain.text: Two angels arrived at Sodom in the evening. Lot was sitting at the city gate. He welcomed them and insisted they stay at his house, where he made them a meal. Before they went to bed, all the men of Sodom, young and old, surrounded the house and demanded that Lot bring the visitors out so they could abuse them. Lot went out and begged them not to do such a wicked thing, and even offered his daughters instead, a terrible offer. The men pushed forward to break down the door, but the angels pulled Lot inside and struck the men with blindness.

The angels told Lot to get his family out, because the LORD was about to destroy the city. Lot's future sons-in-law thought he was joking. At dawn the angels urged Lot to hurry, but he hesitated. Because the LORD was merciful to them, the angels took Lot, his wife and two daughters by the hand and led them out of the city. "Run for your lives! Don't look back." Lot asked to flee to a small town nearby, Zoar, and they agreed.

Then the LORD rained down burning sulphur on Sodom and Gomorrah and destroyed those cities and the whole plain. But Lot's wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt. Early the next morning, Abraham looked down towards Sodom and saw dense smoke rising like smoke from a furnace. God remembered Abraham, and brought Lot out of the catastrophe.

Lot and his two daughters, afraid to stay in Zoar, lived in a cave in the mountains. Thinking there was no man left to give them children, the daughters got their father drunk on two nights and each slept with him without his knowing. Both became pregnant. The older daughter's son was Moab, father of the Moabites, and the younger's son was Ben-Ammi, father of the Ammonites.

summary.bigIdea: God judges the violent wickedness of Sodom but mercifully rescues Lot, though Lot's family story remains broken.
points: The men of Sodom try to abuse Lot's guests.
Out of mercy, the angels lead Lot's family out; Lot's wife looks back.
Sodom and Gomorrah are destroyed; the chapter ends with a sad story in Lot's family.
summary.reflection: God was merciful even to hesitating Lot. What does that tell you about God's patience?
